items.question: In what order are the rows written?
items.chose: Sorts rows by creation time ascending, then by id.
items.instead: Keep the input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: How are ties on creation time ordered?
items.chose: Breaks ties by id, comparing UTF-16 code units (not locale-aware).
items.instead: Keep the input order for ties (stable sort), or compare ids with locale collation.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has bad data (unknown status, negative or fractional counts, filled over openings, invalid date)?
items.chose: Throws an Error that names the requisition id, so no CSV is produced.
items.instead: Skip the bad row, or write it as-is or with blank fields.

items.question: Which statuses are valid?
items.chose: Allows only open, on_hold, filled and cancelled, and throws on any other value.
items.instead: Pass any status string through unchanged.

items.question: Are zero openings or zero filled allowed?
items.chose: Accepts any whole number of at least 0 for both.

items.question: Can filled exceed openings?
items.chose: Throws when filled is greater than openings.
items.instead: Export the row unchanged, since over-filling may be real.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Produces the BOM and header row only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: What are the column names and their order?
items.ticket: Export requisition list to CSV (with status and fill counts)
items.chose: Writes the columns Requisition ID, Title, Status, Openings, Filled, Created.
items.instead: Use other header labels, snake_case names, or add a computed column such as unfilled count.

items.question: What line terminator and file prefix does the CSV use?
items.chose: Ends every row, including the last, with CRLF, and starts the file with a UTF-8 BOM.
items.instead: Use LF with no BOM, and no trailing newline.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD), or a localized format.

items.question: How is a missing or null title written?
items.instead: Throw, or write a placeholder such as "(untitled)".

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped, and are spreadsheet formula prefixes (=, +, -, @) neutralized?
items.chose: Quotes per RFC 4180 and doubles inner quotes. It does nothing about formula-leading characters, and it doesn't quote the status field.
items.instead: Also prefix formula-leading values with a single quote to prevent CSV injection.
